PricingPage.metadata-description: Compare Nakafa Free and Pro for learning materials, practice questions, Nina AI tutoring, and online Tryouts.
PricingPage.headline: Start with Free. <mark>Move to Pro when you are ready.</mark>
PricingPage.description: Compare both plans, then choose the one that fits how you learn.
PricingPage.q1: What can I learn on Nakafa?
PricingPage.a1: Nakafa offers material from primary school through university, including Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, AI, and Data Science. Availability follows the curricula and material already published.
PricingPage.q2: How do I learn with Nakafa?
PricingPage.a2: Start with a lesson, continue with practice questions or a Tryout, then ask Nina about anything you still do not understand.
PricingPage.q3: Are there practice questions with explanations?
PricingPage.a3: Yes. Practice questions include explanations so you can understand the process, not just see the final answer.
PricingPage.a4: Nina can explain concepts, answer questions about a lesson, and help when you get stuck. Everyone uses the same Nina, and one answer uses 5 credits.
PricingPage.a5: Yes. Take and retake any tryout for free, without limits. Scores are included, with IRT scores on supported sets. Nakafa Pro opens the detailed solutions, including for earlier attempts.
PricingPage.q6: Can I learn without creating an account?
PricingPage.a6: Yes. Public learning materials can be read without an account. Sign-in is required to save progress, use AI credits, take a Tryout, and activate Pro.
PricingPage.a7: Yes. Teachers and students use the same lessons, practice questions, and Tryouts as everyone else. If your school needs something more, write to us.
PricingPage.q8: Can I check the sources behind Nakafa material?
PricingPage.a8: Yes. Lessons can include references, and the Markdown source is available when you want to inspect the content or suggest an improvement.
PricingPage.a9: AI credits are used when Nina answers you. Everyone uses the same Nina, and one answer uses 5 credits.
PricingPage.a10: Free credits reset each day. Pro credits reset at the start of each month.
PricingPage.a11: No. Each reset starts a new credit period, so unused credits do not carry over.
PricingPage.q12: What happens when I run out of AI credits?
PricingPage.a12: Nina becomes available again after your next reset or when you move to Pro. Learning materials and practice questions remain available.
PricingPage.q13: Does a failed Nina answer use credits?
PricingPage.a13: No. If Nina cannot complete an answer, no credits are deducted.
PricingPage.a14: Yes. Sign in before payment so Pro can be linked to your Nakafa account. Pro is billed monthly and continues until you cancel it.
PricingPage.q15: How do I manage or cancel Pro?
PricingPage.a15: Sign in, select the Pro button, then manage or cancel your subscription through the customer portal.
PricingPage.a16: Your account returns to Free and receives the daily Free credit allowance.
PricingPage.q17: Will basic learning materials stay free?
PricingPage.a17: Yes. Nakafa's basic learning materials remain free for everyone.
PricingPage.q18: Which curricula are available on Nakafa?
PricingPage.a18: Nakafa includes the Merdeka Curriculum, Cambridge International, Singapore MOE, and a pathway aligned with United States standards. The material you can choose follows the curriculum sections already published.
PricingPage.q19: Can I use Nakafa to prepare for an exam?
PricingPage.a19: Yes. Review concepts with learning materials, check your understanding with practice questions, and rehearse the exam format with Tryouts. Available sets vary with the exams currently published.
PricingPage.q20: Can I use Nakafa on my phone?
PricingPage.a20: Yes. Nakafa works in a browser on phones, tablets, and computers without installing an app.

Faq.q4: What subjects and grades do you cover?
Faq.a4: We cover K-12 through university. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Computer Science, and more. From elementary basics to advanced university courses.
Faq.q7: How does Nakafa ensure content accuracy?
Faq.a7: All content is created by qualified contributors and reviewed by the community. Our source-available approach means anyone can inspect materials and propose improvements. Practice exercises include explanations so you learn from mistakes, not just scores.

atom.title: Atomic Shell Model
atom.description: This diagram uses the simple shell model for neutral atoms up to calcium. It focuses on reading the outer shell and separating the shell content from the maximum <math>2n^2</math> capacity.

neon.name: Neon
neon.note: Its configuration is <math>2, 8</math>. Shell <math>\mathrm L</math> is the outer shell.

magnesium.name: Magnesium
magnesium.note: After shells <math>\mathrm K</math> and <math>\mathrm L</math> are filled, the remaining <math>2</math> electrons enter shell <math>\mathrm M</math>.

chlorine.name: Chlorine
chlorine.note: Its outer shell contains <math>7</math> electrons in this simple shell model.

argon.name: Argon
argon.note: The introductory pattern is <math>2, 8, 8</math>, so shell <math>\mathrm M</math> contains <math>8</math> electrons.

potassium.name: Potassium
potassium.note: Potassium has the element symbol <math>\mathrm K</math>. That is different from shell <math>\mathrm K</math>. After <math>2, 8, 8</math>, the remaining <math>1</math> electron enters shell <math>\mathrm N</math>.

calcium.name: Calcium
calcium.note: Calcium has <math>20</math> electrons, so its simple shell pattern is <math>2, 8, 8, 2</math>.

bacteria.title: Comparing bacterial shape, cell contents, and cell wall
bacteria.description: The model separates outer shape, prokaryotic contents, and cell-wall layers. Rotate the model to see the arrangement of each part from different sides.

shape.caption: In the starting view, the forms from left to right show coccus, bacillus, and spiral bacteria as early recognition clues.
shape.focus: Shape gives the first clue about bacterial morphology. Other evidence completes the identification.
shape.takeaway: Strong identification uses outer form together with other traits.

inside.caption: The nucleoid contains bacterial DNA, while ribosomes are spread through the cytoplasm to make proteins.
inside.focus: There is no membrane-bound nucleus, but DNA and ribosomes are still present.
inside.takeaway: A bacterium stays alive because its membrane, cytoplasm, DNA, ribosomes, and metabolism work together.

wall.caption: In the starting view, the left stack shows a thicker Gram-positive wall, while the right stack shows a Gram-negative wall with an outer membrane.
wall.focus: Compare peptidoglycan thickness and the presence of an outer membrane.
wall.takeaway: Cell-envelope structure affects shape, protection, Gram staining, and sensitivity to some antibiotics.
